moments.body: Google open-sources Kubernetes in 2014, based on internal Borg. The Cloud Native Computing Foundation (2015) becomes the steward. Kubernetes wins the orchestration wars against Docker Swarm and Apache Mesos. By 2024 it's the de facto cloud-native deployment platform.
moments.takeaway: Google open-sourced internal infrastructure on purpose, knowing it would shape competitor adoption. Strategic open source is now corporate playbook.

now.title: Cloud-native today
now.body: Kubernetes runs at most large enterprises. Serverless (AWS Lambda, etc.) competes for some workloads. Service meshes (Istio, Linkerd) add complexity. DevOps culture (developer + operations) and SRE (Google, 2003) reshape how software is operated.
now.open_questions: Has Kubernetes complexity grown beyond utility for most workloads? Platform engineering movement attempts to wrap it.

items.reflection: The cloud-native ecosystem has accumulated over 200 projects under CNCF. The complexity is real; so is the productivity gain when used well. Tradeoffs depend on team scale.

moments.title: Stack Overflow launches
moments.body: Stack Overflow launches in September 2008 as a Q&A site for programmers. Within a year it's the de facto solution lookup for any error message. Reputation-based community moderation, strict closure policies and the 'XY problem' culture shape developer interactions for over a decade.
moments.takeaway: A single Q&A site became the global shared memory of professional programming. Most developers consult it daily.

moments.title: GitHub Copilot
moments.body: GitHub Copilot launches in June 2021 as a preview, becoming general availability in June 2022. It uses OpenAI Codex (fine-tuned GPT-3) to suggest code completions. Lawsuits over training on open-source code (Doe v. GitHub) test the legal limits. Stack Overflow visits decline sharply after ChatGPT (2022).
moments.takeaway: AI code completion went from research curiosity to ~50% of accepted code lines for some developers within three years.

now.title: Developer tools today
now.body: AI coding assistants (Copilot, Cursor, Codeium, Cody, Claude Code) are widely used. The shift from 'manual coding with search' to 'AI-assisted coding with prompting' is the largest developer workflow change since the IDE. Stack Overflow has partnered with OpenAI to license its data.
now.open_questions: How do junior developers learn when AI is doing the typing? Skill formation under AI tooling is a live concern.

items.reflection: The same body of open-source code that built the careers of millions of programmers is now training models that some say will reduce the need for those programmers. The economy of knowledge in software is in a strange new phase.

moments.title: Attention Is All You Need
moments.who: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, et al., Google Brain
moments.body: The Transformer architecture paper at NeurIPS 2017 replaces recurrent networks with a pure attention mechanism for sequence processing. Training parallelises far better. The architecture becomes the substrate of GPT, BERT, T5, LLaMA, Claude, Gemini — essentially all modern frontier AI.
moments.takeaway: A single architectural paper from 2017 underlies almost all the AI products you've used in 2025.

moments.title: GPT-3 and emergent capabilities
moments.body: GPT-3 (175 billion parameters, June 2020) demonstrates 'in-context learning' — answering tasks from few-shot examples without fine-tuning. The paper 'Language Models are Few-Shot Learners' suggests scaling alone produces qualitatively new abilities. The scaling laws (Kaplan et al. 2020; Chinchilla 2022) shape industry investment.
moments.takeaway: Capabilities emerging from scale alone reshaped AI development from feature-engineering to capital-investment. Training a frontier model now costs over $100 million.

now.title: Frontier AI today
now.body: OpenAI's GPT-4, Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini, Meta's LLaMA, xAI's Grok, DeepSeek and Mistral compete on frontier capability. Training runs in 2024-25 cost hundreds of millions of dollars. Inference at scale is becoming the limiting factor. Multimodal (vision, voice, video) and agentic systems are the current frontier.
now.open_questions: Will scaling continue to produce capability gains? Or will architecture-level innovation matter more again? Reasoning models (o1, o3) suggest new gains via inference compute.

items.reflection: Most of the original Transformer paper authors left Google to found AI companies (Adept, Cohere, Character.AI). The talent flow tells the story of where the action moved. Google's most influential paper of the decade was authored by people no longer there.
